solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unfortunate problem is, hotel is blocking plan

indicators.note: the two pieces sit in the way of the plan, lodged in its middle

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a hotel is getting in the way of their development plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, a small misfortune or setback.

clue.text: In Berlin, I must get hold of tablet, running water and freezer

indicators.note: the German pronoun has to take in the tablet

parts.note: ich is German for I
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A German needs a pill, running water and a fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England, often used for river clues.
explanation.definitionFit: An icehouse was a building where ice was stored to keep food cold, an early freezer.

clue.text: Honourable act has always remained a key, if rare, ideal primarily

indicators.note: the first letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A sentence about a noble deed that has always been a rare ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual suicide by disembowelment was the samurai's honourable death to avoid disgrace.

clue.text: Reconciled glib revolutionary party

parts.note: a pat answer is glib, too ready
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A slick revolutionary group has made up its differences.
explanation.definitionFit: Patched up, said of a quarrel, means settled or made up for the time being.

clue.text: End up with one novel still in its wrapping

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A reader ends up with a novel that has never been taken out of its cellophane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; the anagram fodder is END UP plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still wrapped has never been opened, the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Simple duties can, mixed with this absorbing work

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the word for work
duties can and this are jumbled together

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Simple duties can be combined with absorbing work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' makes UNSHISTICATED from the two pieces of fodder; 'absorbing' looks like 'engrossing' but signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated means naive or plain, lacking worldly refinement.

clue.text: Old songwriter exiles son, handy expert?

indicators.note: drives out the letter for son

parts.note: King David, the psalmist, wrote songs, the Psalms

explanation.surface: A hymn writer of old banishes his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy' plays on hands: a palm reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmist reads hands, so is an expert in matters of the hand, playfully handy.

clue.text: Honeymooner in Cornish port docked with journalist

indicators.note: the last letter of the port is cut off, as a tail is docked

parts.note: Newlyn is a fishing port in Cornwall
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A honeymooning couple in a Cornish harbour tied up with a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship in port but means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymooner is someone just married, on the holiday after the wedding.

clue.text: Call for one in Times maybe with bottle

indicators.note: the call stands in place of the one

parts.note: The Times is an example of a daily newspaper
I is the Roman numeral one
to ring is to call by phone

explanation.surface: A call for someone to appear in The Times, maybe with a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for nerve, so acting with bottle is acting boldly.

clue.text: Car capital? Nothing's left, just endless rubble

indicators.note: the zero has left, i.e. departed from the city's name

parts.note: Detroit is the capital of the US motor industry
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: just loses both its ends, keeping its middle letters

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that the old motor city has been reduced to ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing's left' reads as 'nothing remains', but it is O departing from DETROIT; 'endless' takes US from JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or loose waste material, much like rubble.

clue.text: Phone delivery man left nearer the front

indicators.note: the letter for left is shifted forward in the word for the delivery man

parts.note: in cricket a bowler delivers the ball

explanation.surface: A courier has left his phone near the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blower' is British slang for the telephone; in cricket the bowler bowls each delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is informal British slang for a telephone, from speaking tubes one blew into.

clue.text: Reserves short flight for novel establishment?

parts.note: to book is to reserve
a hop is a short trip by air

explanation.surface: A traveller books a quick hop by plane to somewhere new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel establishment' sounds like a new business but means a place that sells novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookshop is a business that sells novels, a playful reading of the phrase.

clue.text: Brad goes back to collect Times for North African

indicators.note: the reversed word gathers the multiplying word inside it
the word for brad is read backwards

parts.note: a brad is a thin small-headed nail
times as in multiplication, two by three

explanation.surface: Someone called Brad returns to fetch a copy of The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A Libyan is a native of Libya, a country of North Africa.

clue.text: Warning sign on entrance: "No English!"

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: no English means the letter for English is removed

parts.note: to entrance is to delight

explanation.surface: A notice on a door bans the English language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway but is the verb, to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A red traffic signal warns drivers to stop; danger signals are also red lamps.

clue.text: Hurry off initially for pint, working to make an impression at Ascot

indicators.note: the opening letters of hurry and off
the letters for pint are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off for a pint, working to make a good impression at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofprint is the mark left by a horse's hoof, an impression on the turf.

clue.text: What's worn in Paris maybe by Private Pike back to front

indicators.note: the back half of the name moves to the front

parts.note: Private Pike is the young soldier in the British TV sitcom Dad's Army; his surname is used

explanation.surface: Asks what the hapless soldier from Dad's Army wears, perhaps on backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard; Pike is its youngest member.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat top, the kind of hat seen in Paris.

clue.text: People who give up stocking new bloomers

indicators.note: holding in stock, the quitters contain the new letter

parts.note: those who kick a habit give it up

explanation.surface: Quitters wearing new stockings and bloomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' and 'bloomers' both read as clothing; the first means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are loose knee-length underpants, a kind of women's underwear.

clue.text: Old Jew's harp in need of tuning, I understand

indicators.note: the harp's letters are out of order

parts.note: I see means I understand

explanation.surface: An old Jew's harp, I gather, needs tuning.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jew's harp is a small twanged mouth instrument, the surface's false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were an ancient Jewish sect known for strict observance of the law.

clue.text: I delay every so often; it's how I behave?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of delay are taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A procrastinator confesses to putting things off now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter of 'delay' gives DLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who delays acts lazily, without urgency, so this is how such a person behaves.

clue.text: Unwilling to work at home, act fast

parts.note: in means at home
to do is to act
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to work stays at home but must act quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like quick but is the fast of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means lazy, idle, averse to effort.

clue.text: Fancy Gilbert, heading off to his work

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means fanciful, so the letters are rearranged
Gilbert's first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A fancy dress Gilbert heads off to his workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' acts on ILBERT, which becomes LIBRET; W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for Sullivan's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert wrote the texts of the Savoy operas, each a libretto set by Sullivan.

clue.text: Old hacker's target presently, PM admitted

indicators.note: the prime minister is let into the word for presently

parts.note: presently means soon
Pitt (Elder or Younger) was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: A computer hacker's next target is soon to be the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacker' suggests computers but means someone with a hacking cough.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon was a bowl that someone with a cough would spit into, now outdated.

clue.text: Very important if dropped from cup tie?

indicators.note: if is taken out of the match

parts.note: a semifinal is a cup tie a stage before the final

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cup tie is very important if a player is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' seems to be a conjunction but is the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminal means highly influential, shaping later developments.

clue.text: Metal business enlists personnel with this writer

indicators.note: the company takes the personnel department into its ranks

parts.note: CO is short for company
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A metals firm hires staff together with the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromium, commonly called chrome, is a hard shiny metallic element.

clue.text: Trophy goes to poet defending love in press

parts.note: a cup is a trophy

indicators.note: the poet surrounds and guards the zero

parts.note: a bard is a poet
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sports trophy goes to a poet who defends love, as reported in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers but is an old word for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a large cupboard for linen or clothes, chiefly in older or Scottish use.

clue.text: Relaxing, each succeeded in golf

parts.note: S is short for succeeded, as in genealogies
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Each player won while unwinding with a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing and relaxing both mean slackening or loosening something.

clue.text: Preparation for going out to work: better to ignore tips

parts.note: to toil is to work hard

indicators.note: both end letters of better are discarded

explanation.surface: Advice that getting ready for work goes better if you skip the details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' after 'going out' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A toilette is the act of washing, dressing and grooming oneself before appearing in public.

clue.text: Man replaces firm in Caledonia? Part of it

indicators.note: the male pronoun takes the place of the company abbreviation

parts.note: Caledonia is the Latin and poetic name for Scotland
CO is short for company, a firm
he is a man or male

explanation.surface: A man takes the place of a business in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' could suggest the Isle of Man, another island group, but it simply gives HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland Islands lie off the north coast and form part of Scotland.

clue.text: Needlework that's liberated husband as well

indicators.note: has freed the husband, so the H letter is let out

parts.note: that, with 's read as has, the verb of liberated
too means as well

explanation.surface: An embroidery project that has freed a husband too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's liberated husband' means THAT has freed H, leaving TAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a design inked into skin with needles, a kind of needlework.
